text:
Josh Norris has seven points in 22 games for Buffalo, and his ice time is drifting down: 13.1 minutes over his last ten, almost two fewer than before. That is a modest role for a player who scored 34 points in 44 games last season.

The numbers say more of this is bad luck than bad play. With Norris on the ice, the Sabres have scored 8.71 fewer goals than their chances deserve. Five-on-five, Buffalo is roughly even with him on (49% of expected goals, the quality of chances), and he still shoots from dangerous spots. His own finishing is fine: four goals on 4.35 expected.

Evolving-Hockey had him at 1.4 wins above replacement last season, nearly all of it from even-strength offense, which is not what a 1.35 points-per-60 player looks like. Our talent range puts his true scoring rate well above where he sits now. The shot volume is the soft spot (24 in 22 games). We'd watch the minutes: they are the one thing working against him.
